title: Married to the Don to Keep Me Silent - Pilot (workflow test: opening scene, canon-corrected)
logline: An ER doctor watches the man whose arm she just splinted shoot in a parking garage - and becomes the witness he can't leave behind.
style: Painterly illustrated realism, gouache and oil texture, cinematic noir composition, wet reflective concrete, saturated orange sodium light against cold blue shadow, soft film grain. Non-graphic suspense: no blood, no gore, no visible wounds
script:
Heba: Two shots. That's all it took.

Heba: I watched a man slide down the side of a silver sedan with a gun lying near his open hand, and the man standing over him wasn't holding that gun. He was holding a different one. In his left hand.

Heba: His right arm was in the plaster splint I had built for him thirty minutes earlier, in bay fourteen, with my own two hands. [2 second pause]

Lion: Go back inside, Dr. Marlowe. You were never here.

Heba: I was an ER doctor.

Heba: Fifty minutes earlier, he had been my patient. Now I was the only witness, and someone on those stairs was listening.

notes:
CANON CORRECTIONS (checked against the novel, see docs/adaptation/canon_ledger.md): ER arrival 3:05 [p.5], stitches 3:20 [p.8], splint ~3:40 [p.8], two shots 4:10 [p.10]. So the splint was built THIRTY minutes before the shots (not 'forty') and the patient was first treated FIFTY minutes before. Nico's line is 'Go back inside, Dr. Marlowe' [p.11] ('Dottoressa' comes later). The garage is St. Brigid's level 2 at 4:10 a.m. (not 3 a.m.). Ivy is a fourth-year ER resident. Nico does not threaten her: Brancato's people are the danger, so 'the witness he couldn't afford to leave behind' was replaced. Original pilot wording is kept in each segment's original_text. Ivy hears the shots and sees the gun in Nico's LEFT hand afterward; she never sees who fires (Enzo does, p.146-147, 314).
PRODUCT DECISION: the FIRST published video must be a COMPLETE short film with a satisfying ending, optimised for views and viewer satisfaction. Book sales are optional (a light, honest mention at most) - NOT a cliffhanger paywall. This 6-shot pilot is only the opening scene used to test the two-speaker workflow; the finished film still needs its middle and a resolved ending.
EDITORIAL PROPOSAL (not the author's approved text): replaces a closing line that said 'I had just married into a family' - premature, because the wedding happens later in the book.
Original closing wording preserved here as far as it was given to this session: it contained the phrase "I had just married into a family". The full original sentence(s) were NOT supplied - paste them below.
Shot durations are ESTIMATES from word counts until real narration audio exists; run `python -m ofs narration sync` after importing audio.
Voices: Heba = Ivy first-person narrator (female). Lion = Nico dialogue + Nico POV (male). No recordings exist in this repo.
